C1462.title: DAGguise Research on Defending Against Memory Side Channels
C1462.summary: In 2022, an MIT team introduced DAGguise to reduce leakage of program-access timing through shared memory controllers. The design organizes requests in a directed acyclic graph and sends real or dummy memory accesses on a fixed schedule, hiding a program's actual behavior. Simulations indicated that it could resist memory-timing side channels while preserving more sharing efficiency than schemes that dedicate the controller to one program at a time.
